seeds.summary: Adopt one record-envelope pattern across governance/runtime record families.
evidence: Strong recommendation is to use a shared record-envelope pattern across major governance/runtime record families.
Benefit is consistent Ledger/export inspection and reusable search/routing fields.

seeds.summary: Candidate envelope includes identity, scope refs, status/provenance, linkage refs, and summary/detail pointers.
evidence: Candidate fields include record_id, record_kind, project_id, optional run_id.
Candidate scope refs include seam/package/node/attempt/promotion/concern/lane/worktree identifiers.
Additional fields include status, created metadata, supersession, source/artifact/evidence refs, summary, and optional detail_ref.

seeds.summary: Review records should capture review target, reviewer, criteria, findings, verdict, links, and timestamps; findings can update concerns but remain distinct records.
evidence: Review record needs review_id, review kind, scope refs, reviewer identity, criteria/profile, findings summary, concern refs, verdict, linked artifacts/evidence, timestamps.
Rule: review findings may nominate/update concerns, but review records stay distinct from concern records.

seeds.summary: Model corroboration as request/packet plus result, with quorum and participant outputs explicitly represented.
evidence: Corroboration should have corroboration_request/packet and corroboration_result layers.
Packet carries claim/issue, target scope, trigger rationale, evidence/source refs, quorum model, participants.
Result carries participant outputs, quorum result, acceptance status, and downstream implications.

seeds.summary: Represent graph patching as request/result with patch trigger context and generation/path transition outputs.
evidence: Graph patch should include graph_patch_request and graph_patch_result.
Request carries patch point, triggering concern refs, requested structural change, affected generation, requester identity.
Result carries old/new generation, invalidated/new/surviving path refs, and resulting concern/promotion/recovery implications.

seeds.summary: Promotion records should encode promotion class, scope transition, eligibility/blockers, supporting refs, decision, and revocation lineage.
evidence: Promotion classes listed: lane_to_package, package_to_seam, seam_completion.
Promotion record should include source/target scope refs, eligibility state, blockers/concerns, review/corroboration refs, decision outcome, and revocation/reopen lineage.

seeds.summary: Recovery records should define recovery kind, scope, trigger/preconditions, result, linkage, and affected concerns.
evidence: Recovery kinds listed: safe-point restore, restart reconciliation, blocked prerequisite resolution, lane/worktree restore.
Recovery record should include target scope refs, trigger reason, preconditions, result, resulting attempt/run linkage, affected concern refs.

seeds.summary: Use a shared exact state transition record for consequential transitions to reduce bespoke decision-summary fields.
evidence: State transition report fields include from_state, to_state, target object, actor/source, reason, prerequisite refs, downstream obligations.
This is proposed to avoid per-object bespoke decision summary fields.

seeds.summary: Keep records and artifacts separate: records are canonical structured objects; artifacts are linked file/blob outputs.
evidence: Strong recommendation is to keep records and artifacts separate.
Review markdown summary and corroboration packet files are artifacts, while corresponding review/corroboration result are structured records.

seeds.summary: Export contracts should anchor on the record envelope and attach artifacts by reference.
evidence: Export contracts should use record envelope as manifest backbone.
Artifacts/files/blobs should attach by reference rather than replacing record structure.

seeds.summary: Current docs assume many exact record families but leave shapes inconsistent; this impairs search/deep-link/Ledger ergonomics.
evidence: Local docs do not shape exact record families consistently.
Artifacts are more concretely described than governing record objects.
Search, deep links, and exact-record Ledger views remain awkward until shapes are normalized.

seeds.summary: Define shared envelope and minimum exact shapes for review/corroboration/graph-patch/promotion/recovery/state-transition record families.
evidence: Carry-forward fix is shared record-envelope convention.
Carry-forward fix is exact minimum shapes for review, corroboration request/result, graph patch request/result, promotion, recovery, and state transition report.
Carry-forward fix is linking artifacts to records rather than substituting them.

seeds.summary: Do not collapse Evidence vs Artifacts panes, and do not conflate parent-summary artifacts with UI evidence summaries.
evidence: Evidence and Artifacts panes should remain distinct even when linking to same underlying record.
Parent-summary artifacts and UI evidence summaries are not interchangeable.
Stable scope refs in envelopes should improve search and deep-link routing.

seeds.summary: Split export contracts into record export, bundle export, and view export to resolve ambiguity in current export language.
evidence: Current docs mention exports in fragments (bundle/thread/usage-ledger/evidence/storage history) but orchestrator export contracts remain underspecified.
Open questions include canonical manifest, view-shaped vs record-shaped exports, packaging of artifacts/records/references, and handling historical/superseded/removed backing objects.
Recommended split is record export (canonical objects), bundle export (manifest + records + artifacts), and view export (filtered user-facing representation).
